voiceover: A well-built website doesn't actually know your password. When you sign up, it runs your password through a hash function, basically a one-way blender. Same input, same output, but you can't un-blend it back. The site stores only that hash. When you log in, it hashes what you typed and checks whether it matches. That's why "forgot password" sends you a reset link instead of your old password. They don't have it. If a site ever emails you your actual password, it's storing it in a way that can be read. That's a red flag. Part two: why the same password can get different hashes.
